tasks.short: Train and lead seasonal forest workers.

steps.what: Find the current approved planting, fire or recreation-maintenance procedure and check its applicability to the assigned site
Demonstrate seasonal forestry techniques, observe worker practice and lead the actual planting, fire-response or maintenance work
Enter and check actual training attendance, observed competence and further instruction needed after the work
Save the approved actual training record v1 in the learning record

tasks.design: Configure the {DOCS} index by seasonal activity, site and approved version; the technician checks applicability before teaching. Configure {LMS} to reuse the session header while the technician enters actual attendance and competence after observing the work; the final checked record is saved by the technician.
tasks.previous_blocker: Procedures and training records may sit in separate stores.
tasks.enabler_now: Native document filters and session forms can reuse known identifiers.
tasks.still_hard: Live fire conditions and worker competence require direct supervision.
tasks.human_edge: Demonstrating safe technique and recognising when a worker needs help.
tasks.altitude: The week still centres on field instruction and supervision.

reach.learn: Site objectives and limits of the technician's delegated instruction

evidence.claim: Native document filters and session headers can reduce reference hunting and repeated header entry without automating field teaching.

assumptions: Boundary is the technician's preparation, instruction and actual training record, not dispatching firefighting crews. Step shares are provisional work estimates, not measured baselines.
The supervisor supplies activity and site identifiers; the procedure owner maintains version, activity, site applicability and approval status in {DOCS}. Missing metadata is checked manually in s1.

The technician produces actual trainee identifiers, attendance, observed practice and follow-up needs in s2-s3. A roster is not evidence of attendance or competence. The small s3 saving is header reuse only; substantive capture and checking remain.
Every saved version must match the final checked record; edits void approval. The ordinary same-system save earns no saving. Existing system runtime is excluded.
unknowns: Whether procedure metadata and learning records already support these fields
research_questions: How much preparation is repeated reference searching rather than site judgement?

already_counted.description: Capture and check actual training outcomes

incremental.description: Maintain seasonal reference links and session-header defaults

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central 3.6 reference-search plus 1.2 header-entry points less 0.5 upkeep = 4.3. Low assumes references are already quick to find and headers already reused; teaching and competence assessment do not shrink.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Explain and enforce forest and environmental regulations.

steps.what: Look up the current forest, environmental, resource-use and fire-safety regulations for the observed activity and jurisdiction
Observe the actual conduct, decide applicable requirements within delegated authority and explain or enforce them with the person concerned
Write and check the actual incident, regulation explained, action taken and any required escalation in the incident record
Save the exact checked incident record v1 in the internal forest incident system

tasks.design: Configure {DOCS} with jurisdiction, activity and current approved source filters; show the source passage rather than generated legal advice. The forest incident system in {OTHER} reuses site and date headers while the technician supplies and checks actual facts and actions before saving.
tasks.previous_blocker: Rules and local delegation can be hard to find together.
tasks.enabler_now: Versioned reference indexes and native record forms can present relevant material.
tasks.still_hard: Applicability, proportionality and conflict with visitors remain human work.
tasks.human_edge: Explain a requirement clearly and recognise when formal enforcement exceeds delegated authority.
tasks.altitude: Reference searching becomes shorter; field judgement stays with the technician.

reach.learn: Scientific basis and limits of local protection measures

evidence.claim: Versioned document filtering and record-header reuse can support an officer without deciding legal applicability.

assumptions: Boundary includes explaining/enforcing and its incident note. Formal citations, agency reports or escalation sends, if present, need their own final-version approval and action steps; no savings are attributed to them here.
The authorised policy owner produces jurisdiction, activity, effective date, source passage and local delegation fields. Missing or conflicting rules are read manually in s1-s2.

The technician produces actual site/time, observed conduct, people involved, rule relied on and actual action in s2-s3. Native forms only reuse known headers; they do not infer conduct or a legal conclusion.
{OTHER} means the forest incident records system. Shares are provisional. Ordinary same-system save is unchanged; an edit invalidates approval. Existing runtime is excluded.
unknowns: Which local enforcement powers and incident fields apply
research_questions: Does the existing document store already filter current rules by activity and jurisdiction?

already_counted.description: Capture and check actual incident details

incremental.description: Check links and local rule-register mappings when sources change

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central lookup reduction 7 plus header reuse 2 less upkeep 1 = 8. Low assumes most source checks still need manual navigation and only minor headers can be reused; observation, explanation and enforcement retain all time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Patrol forests and parks to protect resources.

steps.what: Check the assigned patrol area, current closures and relevant recent incident locations
Patrol the forest or park, observe actual conditions and take the immediate protective action permitted by the situation and role
Record and check the actual patrol route, observations, damage and actions in the patrol log
Save the exact approved patrol log v1 in the internal patrol record

tasks.design: Configure the existing forest GIS and patrol-record system in {OTHER} to show the assigned area, current closures and recent incidents together. Actual patrolling, protection and log authorship stay with the technician; the same-system save is unchanged.
tasks.previous_blocker: Patrol references may require opening several views.
tasks.enabler_now: A native map view can filter existing dated incident and closure layers.
tasks.still_hard: Presence, observation and response to unexpected damage cannot be inferred from a map.
tasks.human_edge: Notice subtle damage and judge an appropriate immediate response.
tasks.altitude: The technician still spends most time in the field.

reach.learn: How observed damage affects protection priorities

evidence.claim: Native geographic views can combine existing closure and incident layers for patrol preparation.

assumptions: Boundary is reference preparation, actual patrol and its log, not producing a new remote-monitoring service. No radio dispatch or external incident report saving is assumed.

The supervisor supplies assigned boundary and patrol date; authorised staff already record closure geometry, validity and incident location/date in {OTHER}. If absent, s1 checks written notices manually, with less saving.

The technician captures actual route, time, observations and protective actions in s2-s3. Planned routes and old incidents cannot become actual completed patrols. No free sensor feed or recording is assumed.
Shares are provisional, and same-system save carries no saving. Any log edit voids approval; system runtime is excluded.
unknowns: Whether closure and incident layers are already available in one view
research_questions: How much preparation is duplicate navigation rather than reading current conditions?

already_counted.description: Capture and check the actual patrol log

incremental.description: Check map-layer references and date filters

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central preparation reduction 2.4 less 0.4 upkeep = 2. Low assumes layers are already combined or require manual notice checks; no patrol or narrative-capture time is removed.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Map forest tract data in a digital mapping system.

steps.what: Check the actual forest tract observations, coordinate reference, collection date, attribute definitions and mapping purpose
Import and transform the checked forest tract features, join explicit tract identifiers and apply the specified map symbology and layout
Validate the exact candidate forest tract map v1 against source coordinates, tract identity, topology, attribute meaning, scale, legend and known field checks
Save the exact approved forest tract map v1 to the internal GIS project

tasks.design: Configure native import, coordinate transformation, explicit identifier joins and layout presets in the forest GIS in {OTHER}. The technician supplies checked observations and the intended mapping specification, resolves import exceptions and validates the completed map before saving; fixed transformations need no model.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated imports and map formatting may be performed manually.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing GIS tools can store repeatable transformations and layouts.
tasks.still_hard: Wrong coordinate systems, stale observations and misleading map meaning need source and field checks.
tasks.human_edge: Decide whether a map represents the tract well enough for its intended use.

ambition.what: No new survey or land-boundary authority.

tasks.altitude: Less repeated map construction; the technician remains responsible for source quality and interpretation.

reach.task: Use forest inventories to plan management
reach.learn: Inventory precision and how map scale affects management decisions

evidence.claim: Native GIS import, coordinate transformation, identifier joins and layout presets can repeat explicitly specified map preparation.

assumptions: Boundary is mapping supplied actual forest data; any new survey collection remains separate human work and is not credited as saved. Step shares are provisional, not a measured inventory baseline.

Survey staff produce actual geometry/coordinates, coordinate reference, tract identifier, observation date, attributes and units. The technician checks them in s1; missing identifiers or metadata are resolved manually, not guessed.

The mapping owner specifies target coordinate reference, join key, allowed attribute codes, scale and legend. s2 uses native saved operations first and retains 40% for running, checking imports and resolving exceptions.
The final map must exist before s3 approval. Edits void approval. Ordinary same-system save and existing GIS runtime earn no labour saving; no publication or external map send is included.
unknowns: How much mapping is repeated structure rather than new cartographic design
Completeness of source coordinates and identifiers
research_questions: Can the current GIS reproduce transformations and joins without a custom integration?

already_counted.description: Run and check imports and resolve join exceptions
Validate the completed map and its meaning

incremental.description: Maintain import mappings, coordinate-reference tests and layout presets

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central 50 construction hours at 60% reduction gives 30 gross, less 1.5 upkeep = 28.5. Low assumes heterogeneous survey files and bespoke legends leave most imports and layout work manual; source assessment and final map validation keep full effort.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Fieldwork, regulation interpretation and final map validation remain central; repeat reference navigation and map preparation can shrink.
reach: Foresters: connect checked tract maps and observed damage to management priorities
role.ambitious_version: A technician who brings reliable field observations and checked maps to the forester while continuing to teach and protect resources in person.
